question: When an LLM solves prompt variants that violate the apparent algorithm of a known circuit, does it reuse the circuit, change component behavior or recruit a different subgraph?

key_findings.claim: The ablated base IOI circuit performs unexpectedly well on DoubleIO and TripleIO, but its output is less faithful to the full model.
key_findings.evidence: On 200 prompts per format, model/circuit logit differences are 2.118/2.722 for DoubleIO and 1.227/3.174 for TripleIO, producing faithfulness above one; most circuit heads' attention changes by less than 0.1.

key_findings.claim: The apparent generalization is partly an ablation artifact termed S2 Hacking.
key_findings.evidence: Mean-ablation removes input paths other than S2 from duplicate/induction heads, effectively pointing the extracted circuit toward the incorrect subject so inhibition heads suppress it. This artifact is absent in the intact model and in base prompts with only one duplicated name.

key_findings.claim: Newly discovered variant circuits reuse every node and base edge while adding duplicate-token input edges.
key_findings.evidence: DoubleIO and TripleIO retain all 26 nodes and 110 base edges, adding 10 and 20 edges respectively. Their overlap with the base is 100% by node and 91.66%/84.61% by total variant edges, with normalized faithfulness 0.765/0.778.

key_findings.claim: A previous-token head provides an order-sensitive decision signal between duplicated names.
key_findings.evidence: Head 2.2 preferentially attends to the name occurring first; both model and circuit perform better when the indirect object appears first, complicating the simple duplicate-suppression story.

method.core_idea: Stress-test a known mechanistic circuit under task-preserving prompt variations, then separate genuine circuit reuse from artifacts introduced by circuit extraction and ablation.
method.mechanism: Generate DoubleIO/TripleIO prompts, compare full-model and circuit logit differences, inspect attention and confidence ratios, trace S2 Hacking, restore token-level paths, and rerun direct-causal-effect/path-patching discovery.
assumptions: The IOI variants probe the same underlying task rather than a qualitatively different behavior.
Logit difference and normalized faithfulness adequately measure circuit behavior.
Mean ablation and path patching isolate causal paths without severe off-distribution effects.
Attention-based functional labels remain meaningful under prompt changes.

techniques.role: Tests external validity of a circuit beyond its discovery distribution.
Compares token attention in a circuit and intact model.
Finds causal input edges for duplicated tokens.
Measures node and edge reuse across task variants.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 small on base IOI, DoubleIO and TripleIO, with 200 generated prompts per variant.
evaluations.metric: Logit difference, accuracy and circuit/model faithfulness.
evaluations.result: The base circuit overperforms the intact model on variants, revealing a faithfulness failure rather than unqualified generalization.
evaluations.baseline: The original 26-head/110-edge IOI circuit and intact GPT-2 small.

evaluations.metric: Attention deviation, confidence ratio and functional faithfulness with 50-sample confidence intervals.
evaluations.result: Duplicate 3.0, induction 5.5/5.9 and inhibition 8.6 form the main artifact path.
evaluations.baseline: The same heads in the intact model and on base IOI prompts.

evaluations.result: Adding duplicate-IO input paths yields 26-node circuits with 120/130 edges and roughly 0.77 faithfulness.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified base circuit and paths added from irrelevant token positions.

limitations: The study covers one small transformer, one linguistic task and two hand-designed prompt variants.
Generated templates may not reflect natural distribution shift.
Circuit discovery inherits choices about mean ablation, thresholds, metrics and component granularity.
Variant circuits recover only about 0.77 normalized faithfulness, leaving substantial behavior unexplained.
The claimed component functions rely heavily on attention patterns and earlier manual labels.
Some uncertainty intervals use only 50 samples.
failure_modes: A circuit appears highly capable because ablation deletes competing inputs and creates an artificial shortcut.
High node overlap hides materially different computations at the edge, position or feature level.
Prompt ordering correlates with the answer and masquerades as the purported duplicate-suppression algorithm.
Path patching on corrupted activations moves the model off-distribution and misstates causal importance.
reusable_insights: A circuit that outperforms its parent model is a warning sign for extraction-induced behavior.
Generalization audits should report model performance, circuit performance, faithfulness and structural overlap together.
Task variants should directly violate the human-readable circuit story, not merely paraphrase inputs.
Node reuse is weaker evidence than edge-, position- and mechanism-level reuse.
open_questions: Do circuit-reuse patterns persist across models, scales and naturally occurring paraphrases?
Can causal scrubbing or interchange interventions distinguish reuse from ablation artifacts more reliably?
What explains the remaining faithfulness gap in the rediscovered variant circuits?
How should circuit identity be defined when features are polysemantic or position-dependent?

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
competitive_landscape.difference: The original work discovers and validates the IOI circuit on its base distribution; the reviewed paper stress-tests the explanation and uncovers variant-specific reuse and an ablation artifact.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: ACDC automates edge selection and benchmarks recovery of known circuits; the reviewed work focuses on whether a particular circuit and mechanism remain valid across prompt formats.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
competitive_landscape.difference: This study examines a larger model and multiple-choice distribution while warning that component meanings are distribution-specific; the reviewed paper gives a deeper controlled generalization audit of one circuit.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Automated Circuit Discovery in Transformers using Contextual Decomposition
competitive_landscape.difference: CD-T accelerates circuit discovery and benchmarks recovery on IOI and other tasks; it does not itself resolve whether recovered circuits preserve their mechanism under adversarial prompt variants.

novelty_assessment: The strongest contribution is not merely showing circuit overlap but demonstrating that an apparently successful circuit can be less faithful precisely because the evaluation intervention creates S2 Hacking. This is a valuable methodological warning, though broad claims about circuit generalization remain premature from one model and synthetic task family.
reviewer_notes: Read all 16 pages, including prompt construction, S2 trace, path additions, circuit tables and appendices. Four primary circuit-discovery/generalization comparators were checked on 2026-08-23.
